title: InPlaceMigrator.migrateIn dangling forceApprove(staker, balanceOf) contradicts the in-code comment
description: Code-vs-comment contradiction. NatSpec at src/InPlaceMigrator.sol:190-192 claims forceApprove is set to the EXACT slice total and 'never left dangling ... nothing lingers'. The code at :225-226 actually approves balanceOf(address(this)), which exceeds total + Sigma topup, so a residual allowance balanceOf - (total + Sigma topup) is granted to staker after the batch. The comment's invariant is false as written. Not a faithfulness F-XX deviation (it is a code-vs-in-code-comment mismatch, not a deviation from a [story-NNN] stated behaviour).
impact: None. The residual allowance is granted to staker, which is immutable and trusted, so under Law-3 owner-trust no value is at risk; the next migrateIn overwrites the approval (no monotonic accumulation). Pure documentation/hygiene defect surfaced in a visible QA channel (Law-1 recall-beats-tidiness).
attackPath: NatSpec at :190-192 claims forceApprove is set to the EXACT slice total and 'never left dangling ... nothing lingers'.
Code at :225-226 approves balanceOf(address(this)), which exceeds total + Sigma topup.
A residual allowance lingers to staker after the batch -> the comment's invariant is false as written.
Bounded: staker is immutable + trusted -> no value at risk; no exploit.
recommendation: Either forceApprove(staker, total + projectedTopups) to match the comment, or add a trailing forceApprove(staker, 0) after the batch to zero the residual allowance and make the 'nothing lingers' invariant true.
